title: Silas and the Compass
premise: When a government survey team vanishes on the Kestrel River, Captain Beatrix Yarrow is hired to ferry investigator Silas Crane upriver to find them. As the monsoon closes in and her boat takes damage, they discover the team was silenced for uncovering a smuggling operation protected by the very officials who sent them. Betrayed by her own patron and hunted by river pirates in official pay, Beatrix must choose between saving her boat and saving the truth. In the end she runs the flooded gorge to deliver the survey evidence downstream, losing her beloved vessel but gaining a new life — and Silas — on the free water beyond the law's reach.
about_author: Kestrel Vane spent a decade working river freight before turning to writing, and their fiction carries the smell of diesel, rain, and rusted iron. They live in a houseboat with two dogs and an unhealthy knowledge of hydrology.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She pilots her aging riverboat, the Magpie, through low-water season, establishing her intimate knowledge of the river and her debts to a shipping magnate named Corven. Emotional beat: weary competence masking restlessness.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Government Paper
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Silas Crane arrives at her dock with a warrant and a fat purse, hiring her to carry him upriver to a vanished survey camp. She distrusts officials but needs the money. Emotional beat: wary bargain struck.

chapters.title: Gear Without Tracks
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. They reach the abandoned camp: tents intact, instruments left behind, no bodies, no blood. Silas notices the survey maps are missing only one folio. Emotional beat: creeping wrongness.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A drowned crewman surfaces near the camp; Beatrix reads the water and knows he was weighted down, not lost. First hint of murder. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Corven's Favor
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A supply stop reveals Corven's men were seen heading upriver ahead of them. Beatrix realizes her patron may be entangled. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: First Rain
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The monsoon's edge arrives early; they shelter in a fishing village where a child describes armed men burning papers at the old trading post. Emotional beat: the hunt becomes real.

chapters.title: The Trading Post Ash
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. They sift the burned post and recover a half-melted page of survey data showing ore samples from land officially designated empty. Emotional beat: revelation with teeth.

chapters.title: Leak Below the Waterline
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The Magpie strikes submerged debris; Beatrix patches the hull by lamplight while Silas bails. Their first true partnership. Emotional beat: grudging respect kindling warmth.

chapters.title: Pirates in Uniform
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A patrol boat flying government colors boards them, searching for 'stolen documents.' Beatrix lies smoothly and hides the folio in the bilge. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Silas Breaks His Warrant
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. He burns his official orders, admitting his superiors likely ordered the cover-up. He asks Beatrix to take him all the way to the delta press town instead of the nearest fort. Emotional beat: duty inverted into conscience.

chapters.title: The Gorge Road Closed
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Landslides have closed the safe channel; the only way forward is the flooded gorge, impassable until the rain peaks and passes. They must wait out the storm with hunters closing in. Emotional beat: trapped.

chapters.title: Night Ambush at the Anchorage
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Corven's hired gunmen attack at anchor; Beatrix uses the river itself — a flash flood surge — to sweep the attackers away. The Magpie is wounded further. Emotional beat: survival at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Shelter-bound during the storm's height, Silas and Beatrix speak honestly about what each has lost to institutions. They cross the line from allies to something more. Emotional beat: tenderness inside danger.

chapters.title: Corven's Voice on the Wire
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A radio call: Corven offers to forgive her debts if she delivers Silas and the folio. She hears in his voice that he killed the survey team. Emotional beat: betrayal made explicit.

chapters.title: The Folio's Secret
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Deciphering the recovered pages, they learn the missing folio names officials above Corven — proof big enough to matter, and dangerous enough to kill for. Emotional beat: the stakes become systemic.

chapters.title: Running the Gorge
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. With the rain easing but pursuers arriving, Beatrix attempts the flooded gorge at dawn — the run of her life, narrated shot by shot through rapids. Emotional beat: transcendent terror and mastery.

chapters.title: What the River Takes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They survive the gorge but the Magpie founders in the outwash; they salvage the folio, a dory, and almost nothing else. Beatrix grieves her boat like a person. Emotional beat: devastating loss.

chapters.title: Downstream Pursuit
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In the leaking dory they outrun Corven's launch through fog and backwaters, using every trick Beatrix knows. Silas is grazed by a bullet. Emotional beat: desperate flight, love tested.

chapters.title: Corven at the Confluence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Cornered at the confluence, Beatrix lures Corven's launch onto a sandbar she alone can read, stranding him as the river rises. Emotional beat: justice delivered by the river's own hand.

chapters.title: The Delta Press Town
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. They deliver the folio to an independent newspaper and a federal judge honest enough to act. Arrests ripple upstream. Emotional beat: vindication, fragile and incomplete.

chapters.title: A Boat of Her Own, Again
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Weeks later, Beatrix buys a battered hull with reward money and refits it with Silas at the caulking. The river forgives nothing, but it moves on. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into renewal.

chapters.title: Free Water
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Beatrix and Silas cast off together with no patron, no warrant, and no debts — taking a charter to map uncharted channels themselves. Emotional beat: open horizon, earned peace.
